default_answers.evidence: I don't know anything about that.
default_answers.location: I don't spend much time thinking about that place, to be honest.

rules.answer_text: Right, so — I was down the alley end around then. Saw someone in a blue coat come in from the square about a quarter to... no, closer to ten-to. Went towards the cafe's back door. Didn't see the face but — that's Elias Grant's coat, everyone knows it. And later there was this thud from inside. Dull, like a sack of flour going over. I didn't think anything of it. You don't, do you.

claims.summary: Clara Wells says she saw someone in a blue coat — she assumes Elias Grant — enter the alley at about 10:26 and head for the cafe's rear door.
Clara Wells says she heard a dull thud from the cafe's back rooms while she was in the alley, around 10:35.

suggested_followups: Why were you in the alley at that time?

rules.answer_text: From about twenty to eight I was at the clinic — Nadia Cole was taking my blood pressure, of all things. I'd been wound up about the meeting. I left just before eight, waited here at a table, and at ten past I went looking for her myself. I found her.

claims.summary: Marcus Bell says he was at the clinic with Nadia Cole from about 10:19 to 10:39, then waited in the cafe.

suggested_followups: Why were you so wound up?

rules.answer_text: So it's true. Owen Price. She promised me that expansion two years ago — I built my plans on it. If you're asking whether I was angry: yes. Angry enough to demand a meeting. Not angry enough for... whatever you're implying. I was with Nadia Cole when it happened, ask her.

claims.summary: Marcus Bell admits the partnership betrayal gave his a grievance, but points to his clinic alibi.

default_answers.alibi: In my yard. Working. Like every morning.

default_answers.last_seen_victim: Outside the cafe, around seven. We had words. I'm not going to pretend we didn't.
default_answers.relationship: Tries too hard to appear helpful and concerned, but their explanations are riddled with convenient omissions. They constantly point fingers at others' poor judgment rather than focusing on the facts.

rules.answer_text: From a quarter past seven I was in my yard. Timber delivery came — big one. Driver, Col Hartley, was with me signing sheets and unloading until gone eight. Check with them if you don't believe me. I've nothing to hide about where I was.

claims.summary: Priya Shah says she was in her yard with delivery driver Col Hartley from 09:54 until after 10:39.

suggested_followups: What were you and Isabella Reed arguing about at 09:44?

rules.answer_text: Eight thousand. There, I've said the number. They'd have ruined me by lunchtime and called it principle. But I was in my yard with Col when it happened, and thank God for that delivery, because I know how this looks.

rules.answer_text: ...Alright. Please don't take this the wrong way. I was in the alley, for a few minutes, around a quarter to eight. With Clara Wells. We've been seeing each other — Marcus Bell doesn't approve of that kind of thing at the shop, so we keep it quiet. We stood by the back door and talked, that's all. We heard a sort of thud from the cafe side and then a door, and we got nervous someone would see us, so we left. Clara Wells went to her van. I went inside. That's everything, I promise.

claims.summary: Owen Price admits he and Clara Wells were secretly meeting in the alley from about 10:24 to just before 10:39, and heard a thud and a door from the cafe side.

rules.answer_text: Clinic, from ten to seven onwards. And before you ask — Marcus Bell was with me from about twenty to eight until eight. Blood pressure check. He was strung tight over some meeting, but he was in my chair the whole time.

rules.answer_text: I crossed the square about twenty to eight, past the cafe window. Isabella Reed was talking to someone — low, but the window was cracked open. I caught '...storage room, before we open...'. Couldn't see or hear who she was talking to. It only means something now, doesn't it.

claims.summary: Nadia Cole heard Isabella Reed say 'storage room, before we open' to someone at about 10:19.

default_answers.alibi: My bench, six-forty until the scream. Best seat in the village.
default_answers.timeline: On the bench. I see everything from there — well. Nearly everything, it turns out.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Going into their cafe this morning, quarter to seven, same as forty years of mornings.
default_answers.relationship: Nervous and easily flustered. They tend to agree with whoever speaks loudest or most confidently, making them unreliable narrators whose testimony shifts depending on who they are speaking to.
default_answers.location: From my bench you can see the cafe, the fountain, the bookshop and the clinic door. Ask away.

rules.answer_text: Forty years I knew them. And I'll tell you something for nothing: last week, in the cafe, I heard them say to somebody — quiet, but furious, the way they got — 'You have until tomorrow.' Never saw who. Kitchen doorway, my back was to it. But Isabella Reed didn't threaten people for sport. Somebody in this village was living on borrowed time, and I'd say the loan came due.

claims.summary: Ben Carter heard Isabella Reed tell someone 'You have until tomorrow' in the cafe last week, but didn't see who.

suggested_followups: Could it have been a member of staff they was talking to?
How did you two first meet?

rules.answer_text: Elias Grant went out the front just before the quarter hour and turned towards the square. Now here's the thing — he says fountain, I hear. I face that fountain, young detective. My eyes aren't what they were, and I did have my crossword. But I don't recall seeing his at it. Priya Shah, though — you should have heard her this morning. That's your man, I'd stake my pension.

claims.summary: Ben Carter, who faces the fountain from his bench, does not recall seeing Elias Grant at the fountain between 10:24 and 10:39 — though he admits his attention was on his crossword.
Ben Carter insists Priya Shah must be the killer because of the morning argument.

suggested_followups: How sure are you that Elias Grant wasn't at the fountain?
